cards.text: Through Haggai the prophet, the LORD told Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, Joshua, the high priest, and the people that His house lies in ruins while each of them is busy with his own house. That word came on the first day of the sixth month, and the LORD said He had summoned a drought. Now everybody's standing there like me when the smoke alarm goes off and I KNOW it's my batch.

cards.question: Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant of the people have heard the LORD's message through Haggai. What do they do with it?

answers.text: They obey the voice of the LORD
They ask Haggai for more time
They wait for the next harvest

cards.question: The leaders and the people obey the words of the prophet Haggai, because the LORD their God had ___ him.

cards.text: So the people feared the LORD. Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, brings them another message, and this one is SHORT. Friend, I've cracked open fortune cookies with longer fortunes.

cards.question: Haggai brings a short new message from the LORD to the people who just obeyed. What does the LORD say?

cards.text: Then something happens inside the leaders and the people. Their spirits get stirred up, like dough that finally starts to rise after you've been staring at it for an hour.

cards.question: Somebody stirs the spirits of Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people. Who is it?
Only the two leaders get their spirits stirred by the LORD, and the rest of the people just follow along.

cards.text: And with their spirits stirred, they don't schedule a meeting to plan the next meeting. They COME.

cards.question: Their spirits stirred, the people come and begin the work on the ___ of the LORD of Hosts, their God.

cards.text: The text even gives the start date: the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius. I spent YEARS in a drawer waiting for somebody to get around to me, so trust me, I notice a date.

cards.question: Haggai's first message came on the first day of the sixth month. The work on the house of the LORD starts about three months after that.

findings.problem: Card 6 says something happens inside 'the leaders and the people' and that 'Their spirits get stirred up.' This gives away the answer to the true or false on card 8, which asks whether only the two leaders get their spirits stirred.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 7's question says 'Somebody stirs the spirits of Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people.' That rules out True on card 8 before the baker gets there, so card 8 becomes a giveaway. Rework card 8 or the wording on cards 6 and 7.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'They obey the voice of the LORD' uses the passage's Bible phrasing. The wrong answers ('They ask Haggai for more time', 'They wait for the next harvest') are plain modern wording, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'Now everybody's standing there like me when the smoke alarm goes off and I KNOW it's my batch' states as fact that the leaders and people feel caught or guilty. The text gives no feeling at this point. If he keeps the guess, it needs to be marked as his own.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This is the first story card to mention King Darius, but it doesn't say who he is (king of Persia, with reference).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer (False: the work starts about three weeks later, in the same month, not three months later) depends on the first message's date in Haggai 1:1 as well as Haggai 1:15. The card cites only Haggai 1:15.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.
